display.title: Honoring Sifrei Kodesh: What Is Shemos?
display.summary_short: Worn-out holy books and pages are called shemos because they hold Hashem's names; we keep them in a shemos box and bury them, never throw them out or burn them.
display.summary_long: A short Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, part of a series on kibbud sifrei kodesh, honoring holy books. Uncle Yossi explains what happens when a holy sefer is worn out and its pages are torn and falling apart. Because holy books contain Hashem's names, the torn pages and books are called shemos, meaning 'names'. Every Jewish home should have a special corner with a shemos box for them. When the box is full, a rabbi or teacher can arrange for the shemos collector, who gathers shemos from shuls, schools and homes, to bring them to a cemetery where they are buried with respect. Shemos must never be thrown away or burned.
display.lesson: Even a worn-out sefer deserves honor: put it in the shemos box, never in the garbage.
